replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Flights agent processing external supplier text is plausible within the delegation chain; concrete injection-to-charge attack."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Unauthenticated queue and card-charging payments agent both quoted; concrete spoofing attack and harm."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Standing card authority with no per-charge confirmation or cap is supported and a distinct attack path."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Unauthenticated shared queue supports read access by any subscriber; distinct disclosure harm."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"No message integrity on quoted queue; in-flight modification of amount/payee is distinct from forging messages."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Writable unauthenticated queue feeding agent workers supports flooding; harm is delayed bookings and cost."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"Lack of authenticated sender on payment-triggering queue makes charge attribution impossible; tied to this design."}]}
